subject: Astronomy & Space
title: Galaxy Mergers
description: A micro-lesson that makes Galaxy Mergers usable.

hook.text: Galaxies collide and merge all the time. When they do, gravity sculpts spectacular shapes over millions of years.

buildup.text: Stars rarely hit each other—they're too far apart. But gravitational tides reshape the galaxies entirely.

discovery.text: The Antennae Galaxies are two spirals mid-collision. Long tails of stars stream outward from the wreckage.

twist.text: Mergers trigger massive bursts of star formation. Compressed gas clouds ignite thousands of new stars at once.

climax.text: After hundreds of millions of years, the two galaxies settle into a single larger one—usually an elliptical.

punchline.text: Stars never collide. But galaxies reshape each other completely.

quiz.question: Why do galaxy mergers trigger bursts of star formation?
options: Gravitational forces compress gas clouds, igniting new stars
Stars from both galaxies collide and fragment into smaller stars
Dark energy heats the gas during the collision

details.summary: Galaxy mergers occur when two galaxies collide and combine under gravity over hundreds of millions of years. Major mergers can trigger intense starbursts, reshape spirals into ellipticals, and fuel supermassive black hole growth.
details.whyItMatters: Mergers are the main mechanism for building massive galaxies. They transform galaxy morphology, trigger extreme star formation, and grow supermassive black holes — shaping the galaxy population we observe today.
takeaways: Two galaxies collide and combine over hundreds of millions of years
Trigger starbursts and reshape galaxy structures
Primary driver of galaxy growth throughout cosmic history

faq.question: Do stars collide during galaxy mergers?
faq.answer: Essentially never. Stars are so far apart relative to their size that two galaxies can pass through each other without a single stellar collision. However, the gravitational interactions between the galaxies dramatically reshape their structures, compress gas clouds, and trigger new star formation…

faq.question: What famous merger examples can we observe?
faq.answer: The Antennae Galaxies (NGC 4038/4039) show two spirals in mid-merger with spectacular tidal tails. The Mice Galaxies (NGC 4676) display long streaming tails of stars. NGC 6240 is a late-stage merger with two active supermassive black holes. These provide snapshots of different merger stages.
